title: The pH scale: a tenfold step at every unit
caption: pH = −log₁₀[H⁺], with [H⁺] in mol dm⁻³. Each unit of pH is a tenfold change in hydrogen ion concentration, so pH 3 has ten times the [H⁺] of pH 4, not twice. pH 7 is neutral at 25 °C, the stomach is about pH 2 and human blood is kept at pH 7.35 to 7.45.
alt: A coloured bar from pH 0 on the left to pH 14 on the right, labelled acidic and alkaline, with the hydrogen ion concentration under each unit falling from 1 to 10 to the minus 14, markers for the stomach at about pH 2, neutral at pH 7 and blood at 7.35 to 7.45, and a worked example: a tenfold rise in [H⁺] from 10 to the minus 4 to 10 to the minus 3 lowers the pH from 4 to 3.
description: Each pH unit is a tenfold change in [H⁺].
pH 7 is neutral at 25 °C; below 7 is acidic and above 7 is alkaline.
Human blood is kept at about pH 7.35–7.45; the stomach is about pH 2.
Worked example: [H⁺] = 1 × 10⁻⁴ gives pH 4; a tenfold rise to 1 × 10⁻³ gives pH 3.
